"Create a game about an immersive archaeological adventure where players explore vast, sun-drenched landscapes to uncover hidden treasures buried deep beneath the dunes. The core experience focuses on the tactile satisfaction of digging through layers of shifting sand to reveal encrusted artifacts, ranging from ancient gold coins to delicate fossilized remains. Once an item is unearthed, the gameplay shifts to a detailed restoration phase where players use specialized brushes and water tools to carefully scrub away grime and salt buildup, revealing the true luster of their find. These cleaned relics are then appraised and sold to a virtual museum or private collectors, allowing players to reinvest their earnings into high-grade excavation gear and advanced cleaning kits to tackle even rarer, more fragile discoveries. You are an professional game developer and the game needs to look it's best, And make sure the game is specifically for mobile players, so no web scrolling games

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

content.text:
playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key
  sessionstorage-set <key> <value> set a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-delete <key> delete a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage

Network:
  requests                    list all network requests since loading the page. each request is numbered for use with the `request` command.
  request <index>             show full details (headers, body, response) of a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-body <index>       print the response body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command. textual bodies are inlined; binary bodies are saved to a file and the path is printed.
  route <pattern>             mock network requests matching a url pattern
  route-list                  list all active network routes
  unroute [pattern]           remove routes matching a pattern (or all routes)
  network-state-set <state>   set the browser network state to online or offline

DevTools:
  console [min-level]         list console messages
  run-code [code]             run playwright code snippet
  recording-start             start recording user actions
  recording-stop              stop recording user actions and print them as playwright code
  tracing-start               start trace recording
  tracing-stop                stop trace recording
  video-start [filename]      start video recording
  video-stop                  stop video recording
  video-chapter <title>       add a chapter marker to the video recording
  video-show-actions          annotate subsequent cli/mcp actions on the page with a callout that names the action and highlights the target element
  video-hide-actions          stop annotating actions performed on the page
  show                        show playwright dashboard
  pause-at <location>         run the test up to a specific location and pause there
  resume                      resume the test execution
  step-over                   step over the next call in the test
  generate-locator <target>   generate a playwright locator for the given element
  highlight [target]          show (or with --hide, remove) a highlight overlay for an element; `--hide` without a target hides all page highlights.

Install:
  install                     initialize workspace
  install-browser [browser]   install browser

Browser sessions:
  list                        list browser sessions

  kill-all                    forcefully kill all browser sessions (for stale/zombie processes)

Global options:

  for (const row of RANKS) if (renown >= row.at) rank = row.name;
  return rank;
}

export function siteFor(id) {
  return SITES.find(site => site.id === id) || SITES[0];
}

export function artifactFor(id) {
  return ARTIFACTS[id] || ARTIFACTS.dinar;
}

export function levelFor(state, key) {
  return Math.max(1, Math.min(3, state.levels[key] || 1));
}

export function upgradeCost(key, state) {
  const def = UPGRADES[key];
  const level = levelFor(state, key);
  return level >= 3 ? null : def.costs[level];
}

export function cleaningGrade(state) {
  return Math.min(levelFor(state, 'brush'), levelFor(state, 'water'), levelFor(state, 'cloth'));
}

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable, polished mobile archaeological adventure game centered on excavation, artifact restoration, appraisal, selling, and gear upgrades.

## Requirements
- Immersive sun-drenched archaeological landscapes with buried treasures.
- Tactile sand digging with shifting layers.
- Restoration using specialized brushes and water tools.
- Appraise and sell relics to museums or collectors.
- Reinvest earnings into excavation gear and cleaning kits.
- Professional visual quality with a mobile-player-first, no-web-scrolling experience.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a touch-first native-feeling single-screen app with bottom navigation and fixed viewport layout.
- Used procedural Canvas rendering for digging, restoration, and artifact artwork.
- Added procedural Web Audio for ambience and interaction feedback.
- Assumed a 12-relic collection and 620 starting coins.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the main mobile interface, title area, site carousel, wallet, renown, bottom navigation, and modal/toast systems.
- Added multiple excavation sites and procedurally illustrated artifacts.
- Implemented a sand-cover digging interaction with movable tool pressure and relic discovery.
- Implemented the cleaning phase with brush, water, and cloth tools.
- Added artifact appraisal, condition/market/grade presentation, museum and shop flows.
- Added persistent save state, upgrades, procedural audio, swipe site navigation, and touch gestures.
- Added local fonts, icons, journal field notes, favicon, and responsive mobile sizing.

### Active
- (none)

- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run final end-to-end validation across home, digging, lifting, cleaning, appraisal, sale, museum, and shop flows.
2. Test multiple portrait/mobile viewport heights for overflow and button visibility.
3. Verify persisted progress and upgrade purchases from a fresh browser state.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: Main mobile app structure and screen markup.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css`: Complete visual system and responsive layout.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/main.js`: App state, navigation, screens, saves, sales, and upgrades.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/dig.js`: Canvas excavation interaction.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/clean.js`: Canvas restoration interaction.

- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/screenshots/hero.png`: Fine-detail landscape crop screenshot.

## Important Context
- The game uses `localStorage` key `dune_and_dust_save_v3`.
- Global debug access is exposed as `window.__DUNE` for state and screen inspection.
- Changes are uncommitted unless prior repository state differed.

## Dune & Dust — Relic Hunter

A touch-first archaeological adventure built as a single-screen mobile web app. Excavate sun-buried sites, brush and mist relics back to life, appraise them under the loupe, and decide whether to grow the museum or take a collector's coin.

### Play

No build step is required. Serve the repository and open it on a phone-sized viewport:

```bash
python3 -m http.server 3002
# then open http://localhost:3002
```

### The loop

1. **Field** — swipe the site card or tap the rail to choose an expedition, then drag across the trench to sweep sand.
2. **Lift** — once the signal is exposed, lift the find and take it to the restoration lab.
3. **Lab** — dry-brush the grime, mist away the salt crust, then buff the surface with the cloth.
4. **Appraise** — read the condition, market value, and grade, then sell to the Atlas Museum for renown or to a private collector for coin.
5. **Reinvest** — spend earnings at the supply depot on wider trowels, better sieves, sonar, and conservation tools.

Progress saves automatically in `localStorage` under `dune_and_dust_save_v3`. The app is designed to stay within the viewport with no page scrolling, including compact 320 × 568 screens.

## Objective
- Build a complete, polished, mobile-first archaeological adventure game centered on excavation, restoration, appraisal, sales, and gear upgrades.

## Requirements
- Immersive archaeological landscapes, tactile digging, specialized restoration tools, appraisal and museum/collector sales, and reinvestment in gear.
- Professional visuals and a fixed, no-scrolling mobile-player experience.

## Decisions
- Use a single-screen, touch-first app with bottom navigation, procedural Canvas artwork and interactions, and procedural Web Audio.
- Use a 12-relic collection, 620 starting coins, and `localStorage` key `dune_and_dust_save_v3`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented home/site selection, wallet and renown, excavation and restoration screens, appraisal and sale flows, museum, shop, upgrades, save state, audio, and touch/swipe interactions.
- Validated fresh home and excavation at 390×844; digging reached 100% exposure, enabled lifting, and successfully entered restoration.
- At 360×640 and 430×932, home remained within the viewport with no document overflow.
- Restoration brush cleared grime; water removed most salt and advanced to the polish phase.

### Active
- Finish end-to-end validation: cloth polishing, appraisal, sale, museum, shop, purchases, and save persistence.
- Check every screen at multiple portrait viewport sizes for clipped controls or overflow.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue restoration with the cloth tool; verify completion enables appraisal.
2. Complete appraisal, museum/collector sale, museum and shop flows, and verify upgrades and persisted progress from a fresh browser state.
3. Check all screens at short and tall mobile viewports; address any hidden or clipped controls.
4. Review the working tree and preserve the current uncommitted project files.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: App structure and screen markup.
- `styles.css`: Visual system, fixed viewport layout, and responsive sizing.
- `js/main.js`: State, navigation, saves, sales, and upgrades.
- `js/dig.js`: Excavation interaction.
- `js/clean.js`: Restoration interaction and cleaning phases.
- `js/data.js`: Sites, relics, upgrades, and progression data.
- `js/art.js`: Procedural landscape and artifact artwork.
- `js/audio.js`: Procedural ambience and interaction sounds.
- `screenshots/`: Existing screenshots and recent validation captures.

## Important Context
- `window.__DUNE` exposes `state`, `showScreen`, `startDig`, `startClean`, `beginDig`, `sellRelic`, `save`, `digScene`, and `cleanScene` for inspection.
- Browser validation reached cleaning’s `polish` phase; the next action is selecting cloth and sweeping the artifact. The current salt ratio was about 8%, while the UI displayed 0%.
- The working tree contained untracked app files and assets; no app changes had been committed.

## Objective
- Finish and polish the complete mobile-first archaeological adventure game, from excavation through restoration, appraisal, sales, museum collection, shop upgrades, and persistent saves.

## Requirements
- Fixed no-scrolling, touch-first mobile experience with procedural Canvas artwork and Web Audio.
- Preserve the 12-relic collection, 620 starting coins, and `dune_and_dust_save_v3` save key.
- Support museum and collector sales, renown progression, gear upgrades, locked sites, and save persistence.

## Decisions
- Fixed the duplicate museum offer ID collision by introducing `museumOfferRenown` and `museumOfferValue`.
- Added an appraisal market-pulse panel and responsive mobile styling.
- Added a first-find grant of $150 and a three-relic gallery milestone grant of $200.
- Added short-viewport-specific layout rules and proper safe-area tabbar sizing.
- Split local font weights into individual installed font files for consistent rendering.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented and end-to-end validated excavation, lifting, restoration, appraisal, museum and collector sales, museum, shop, and upgrades.
- Verified cloth polishing completes restoration and enables appraisal.
- Verified museum sale awards coins and renown, private sales award only coins, and sale overlays complete correctly.
- Verified first-find and three-relic gallery milestone bonuses.
- Verified trowel upgrades spend coins and persist across reload.
- Verified museum collection totals, renown, grades, and values.
- Verified locked-site messaging for the Obsidian Tomb.
- Verified save persistence for coins, renown, collection, gear level, flags, and current relic state.
- Checked layout at 320×568, 360×640, 375×667, 390×844, 390×760, and 430×932 without clipped controls or document overflow.
- Confirmed duplicate HTML IDs were removed and no browser console errors or JavaScript syntax errors remain.
- Updated `README.md` with the game loop and local launch instructions.

### Active
- (none)

- (none)

1. (none)

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: App structure, screens, appraisal offers, museum UI, and modal markup.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css`: Fixed mobile layout, responsive breakpoints, typography, and visual polish.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/main.js`: State, navigation, saves, appraisal, sales, museum, shop, and progression.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/dig.js`: Excavation interactions and exposure progression.

- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/art.js`: Procedural landscapes and artifact artwork.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/audio.js`: Procedural wind and interaction audio.

## Important Context
- The game has been functionally completed and end-to-end validated, including persistence across reload.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Finish and polish the complete mobile-first archaeological adventure game, including a collection book and expanded site artifact rosters.

## Requirements
- Preserve fixed no-scrolling, touch-first mobile layout, procedural Canvas artwork, Web Audio, and save key `dune_and_dust_save_v3`.
- Preserve the 620 starting coins, persistent state, excavation/restoration/appraisal/sales progression, museum, shop, renown, and locked sites.
- Add a collection book grouped by digging site.
- Show undiscovered artifact entries as black silhouettes/shadows and discovered entries with their artwork.
- The book should communicate how many artifacts exist at each site.
- Add 3–4 more artifacts to each existing digging site.

## Decisions
- Museum and collector sale state, renown, first-find grant, gallery milestone grant, and responsive layout decisions remain in effect.
- Collection book discovered state should be derived from the saved `state.collection` entries, with all site artifact IDs supplying the full roster.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented and end-to-end validated excavation, lifting, restoration, appraisal, museum and collector sales, museum gallery, shop, upgrades, and save persistence.
- Verified cloth polishing enables appraisal and sale overlays complete correctly.
- Verified first-find and three-relic milestone bonuses.
- Verified trowel upgrades persist and museum totals, renown, grades, values, and locked-site messaging work.
- Verified portrait layouts at 320×568, 360×640, 375×667, 390×844, 390×760, and 430×932 without document overflow.
- Verified save key `dune_and_dust_save_v3` and window inspection APIs in `window.__DUNE`.
- Implemented responsive mobile styling, appraisal market-pulse panel, and updated README.

### Active
- Collection book feature is requested but not implemented.
- Site artifact expansions are requested but not implemented.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Expand `SITES[].artifacts` and `ARTIFACTS` with 3–4 additional unique relics for each of the four sites.
2. Add procedural artwork painters for all newly added artifact types or reuse suitable existing painters while assigning distinct names and metadata.
3. Update the museum section or add a dedicated collection-book screen with grouped site pages and progress counts.
4. Render undiscovered relics with a black silhouette/shadow and discovered relics with their actual procedural artwork.
5. Update `TOTAL_RELICS` and home/museum recovered totals from the expanded artifact roster.
6. Verify collection discovery persistence, site grouping, shadow artwork, layouts, and the complete digging-to-book loop.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: App structure and museum UI; add collection-book markup/navigation here.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css`: Add collection-book and silhouette/discovered-card styling.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/data.js`: Expand `SITES`, `ARTIFACTS`, and `TOTAL_RELICS`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/main.js`: Add collection-book rendering, discovery lookup, navigation, and totals.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/art.js`: Add or reuse artifact painters and render artwork for book entries.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/README.md`: Document the collection book and expanded game roster.

## Important Context
- Existing files remain uncommitted: `README.md`, `index.html`, `styles.css`, `js/main.js`, `js/clean.js`, `js/data.js`, and possibly other prior work.
- Existing collection is stored as saved objects containing `artifactId`, `condition`, `value`, and `buyer` in `state.collection`.
- Existing art uses `drawArtifact(ctx, artifact.art, ...)`; the collection book can generate images through the existing `artifactImage` path.
- Window inspection remains available through `window.__DUNE` with `state`, `showScreen`, `startDig`, `startClean`, `beginDig`, `sellRelic`, `save`, `digScene`, and `cleanScene`.

21: ## Dune & Dust — Relic Hunter
22: 
23: A touch-first archaeological adventure built as a single-screen mobile web app. Excavate sun-buried sites, brush and mist relics back to life, appraise them under the loupe, and decide whether to grow the museum or take a collector's coin.
24: 
25: ### Play
26: 
27: No build step is required. Serve the repository and open it on a phone-sized viewport:
28: 
29: ```bash
30: python3 -m http.server 3002
31: # then open http://localhost:3002
32: ```
33: 
34: ### The loop
35: 
36: 1. **Field** — swipe the site card or tap the rail to choose an expedition, then drag across the trench to sweep sand.
37: 2. **Lift** — once the signal is exposed, lift the find and take it to the restoration lab.
38: 3. **Lab** — dry-brush the grime, mist away the salt crust, then buff the surface with the cloth.
39: 4. **Appraise** — read the condition, market value, and grade, then sell to the Atlas Museum for renown or to a private collector for coin.
40: 5. **Reinvest** — spend earnings at the supply depot on wider trowels, better sieves, sonar, and conservation tools.
41: 
42: Progress saves automatically in `localStorage` under `dune_and_dust_save_v3`. The app is designed to stay within the viewport with no page scrolling, including compact 320 × 568 screens.

## Objective
- Finish and polish the mobile-first archaeological adventure game, including a collection book and expanded artifact rosters for each digging site.

## Requirements
- Preserve the fixed, no-scrolling, touch-first mobile layout, procedural Canvas artwork, Web Audio, and save key `dune_and_dust_save_v3`.
- Preserve the existing progression and economy, including 620 starting coins, persistent state, excavation/restoration/appraisal/sales, museum, shop, renown, and locked sites.
- Add a collection book grouped by digging site, showing each site's artifact count; undiscovered artifacts should appear as black silhouettes and discovered artifacts with their artwork.
- Add 3–4 artifacts to each existing digging site.

## Decisions
- Derive discovered status from saved `state.collection` entries and use each site's artifact IDs as the full roster.
- Reuse existing procedural painters where appropriate while giving new artifacts distinct names and metadata.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented and end-to-end validated excavation, lifting, restoration, appraisal, museum and collector sales, museum gallery, shop, upgrades, and save persistence.
- Verified cloth polishing enables appraisal, sale overlays, first-find and three-relic milestone bonuses, and trowel upgrade persistence.
- Verified museum totals, renown, grades, values, locked-site messaging, and responsive layouts at 320×568, 360×640, 375×667, 390×844, 390×760, and 430×932.
- Updated README, responsive mobile styling, and appraisal market-pulse panel.

### Active
- Implement the collection book and expand the artifact rosters for all four existing digging sites.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the complete site and artifact definitions in `js/data.js`; add 3–4 unique relics per site and update `TOTAL_RELICS`.
2. Add procedural artwork painters or reuse suitable existing painters for new artifact types.
3. Add a collection-book view grouped by site, with per-site progress counts and discovered/undiscovered artwork states.
4. Update recovered totals and document the feature in the README.
5. Verify collection persistence, site grouping, silhouette rendering, mobile layouts, and the digging-to-book flow.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Screen markup and navigation; museum section is around lines 476–496.
- `js/data.js`: `SITES`, `ARTIFACTS`, and `TOTAL_RELICS`.
- `js/main.js`: Screen navigation, museum rendering, saved collection lookup, and totals.
- `js/art.js`: Procedural artifact painters and artwork helpers.
- `styles.css`: Mobile layout and screen styling.
- `README.md`: Existing game documentation.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; prior modified files include `README.md`, `index.html`, `styles.css`, `js/main.js`, `js/clean.js`, and `js/data.js`.
- Saved collection entries contain `artifactId`, `condition`, `value`, and `buyer`; the save key is `dune_and_dust_save_v3`.
- `drawArtifact(ctx, artifact.art, ...)` and the existing `artifactImage` path can render procedural artwork. `drawArtifactShadow` already exists for excavation visuals.
- The guaranteed first find is `dinar` at site index 1; preserve that behavior when expanding rosters.
- `window.__DUNE` exposes `state`, `showScreen`, `startDig`, `startClean`, `beginDig`, `sellRelic`, `save`, `digScene`, and `cleanScene` for inspection.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Finish and polish the mobile-first archaeological adventure game, including a collection book and expanded artifact rosters for every digging site.

## Requirements
- Preserve fixed, no-scrolling, touch-first mobile layout, procedural Canvas artwork, Web Audio, save key `dune_and_dust_save_v3`, and existing excavation/restoration/appraisal/economy progression.
- Add 3–4 artifacts to each existing digging site and a collection book grouped by site.
- Show undiscovered artifacts as black silhouettes and discovered artifacts with their artwork.
- Preserve the 620 starting coins, persistent state, museum, shop, renown, locked sites, and existing upgrade behavior.
- Preserve the guaranteed first find as `dinar` at site index 1.

## Decisions
- Collection discovery is derived from `state.collection` entries, with each site's artifact IDs defining the full roster.
- New artifacts should reuse suitable existing procedural painters and receive distinct names and metadata.
- The museum remains as the featured-acquisition/gallery view; the collection book should be added separately.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented excavation, lifting, restoration, appraisal, museum and collector sales, gallery, shop, upgrades, and save persistence.
- Verified cloth polishing, appraisal/sales overlays, first-find and three-relic bonuses, trowel persistence, market-pulse panel, and locked-site messaging.
- Verified fixed mobile layouts at 320×568, 360×640, 375×667, 390×844, 390×760, and 430×932.
- Updated README and responsive styling.
- Inspected complete site and artifact definitions and identified existing compatible painters.

### Active
- Add 3–4 unique relics per digging site and raise `TOTAL_RELICS`.
- Add procedural artwork selection or reuse existing painter IDs for new artifacts.
- Implement the collection-book view grouped by digging site with discovered counts and silhouette rendering.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Update `SITES[].artifacts`, `ARTIFACTS`, and `TOTAL_RELICS` in `js/data.js`.
2. Add or reuse procedural painters in `js/art.js` for the expanded roster.
3. Add collection-book markup and grouped, per-site rendering in `index.html` and `js/main.js`.
4. Update total relic values, counts, and README documentation.
5. Verify save persistence, first-find behavior, silhouette/discovered states, site grouping, and mobile digging-to-book flow.

## Relevant Files
- `js/data.js`: Site rosters, artifact metadata, totals, rank progression, and artifact lookup.
- `js/art.js`: `PAINTERS`, `drawArtifact`, `drawArtifactShadow`, and procedural artifact rendering.
- `js/main.js`: Museum rendering, navigation, state collection lookup, totals, digging selection, and save persistence.
- `index.html`: Museum markup and navigation structure.
- `styles.css`: Museum and fixed mobile page layout styles.
- `README.md`: Existing game documentation.

## Important Context
- Changes remain uncommitted.
- Saved collection entries contain `artifactId`, `condition`, `value`, and `buyer`.
- `window.__DUNE` exposes `state`, `showScreen`, `startDig`, `startClean`, `beginDig`, `sellRelic`, `save`, `digScene`, and `cleanScene`.
- `artifactImage(id, size)` and `drawArtifact(ctx, artifact.art, ...)` are the existing artwork paths.
- `drawArtifactShadow` is available for excavation silhouettes and shadow rendering.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Finish and polish the mobile-first archaeological adventure game with an expanded collection book and larger artifact rosters at every digging site.

## Requirements
- Preserve the fixed, no-scrolling, touch-first mobile layout, procedural Canvas artwork, Web Audio, save key `dune_and_dust_save_v3`, and existing excavation/restoration/appraisal/economy progression.
- Preserve 620 starting coins, persistent state, museum, shop, renown, locked sites, upgrade behavior, and the guaranteed first find of `dinar` at site index 1.
- Add 3–4 unique relics per existing site and raise `TOTAL_RELICS`.
- Discovery is derived from `state.collection`; each site's `artifacts` array defines its full roster.
- Undiscovered artifacts appear as black silhouettes; discovered artifacts show their procedural artwork.
- Keep the museum as the featured-acquisition/gallery view and add collection-book markup separately.

## Decisions
- Expanded each site roster from 3 to 6 artifacts, bringing the intended total to 24 relics.
- New artifacts reuse suitable existing painter IDs rather than introducing incompatible artwork.
- Collection state entries remain keyed by `artifactId`, `condition`, `value`, and `buyer`.
- The collection book is to be grouped by digging site and show per-site discovered counts.

## Work State
### Completed
- Confirmed and inspected the complete site and artifact definitions and existing compatible painters.
- Added four new IDs to the Sunken Caravan roster and metadata for six expanded-caravan/temple roster entries.
- Added 3–4 metadata entries for each subsequent site roster.
- Updated all 4 existing site rosters to six artifacts each.
- Set the broader roster toward 24 artifacts.
- Preserved the museum, gallery, economy, progression, and save behavior.
- Verified existing mobile layouts and gameplay flows in prior work.

### Active
- Replace the remaining pending roster implementations, collection rendering, and UI polish.
- Update `TOTAL_RELICS` to 24 and all museum/count labels.
- Implement grouped collection-book markup and rendering.

### Blocked
- None.

## Next Move
1. Update `TOTAL_RELICS = 24` in `js/data.js`.
2. Implement a collection-book section/screen grouped by `SITES` with discovered totals.
3. Render undiscovered IDs using `drawArtifactShadow`-style or solid-black silhouette treatment.
4. Render discovered IDs through `artifactImage(id, size)` or `drawArtifact(...)`.
5. Add collection-book navigation within the museum while preserving existing museum tabs.
6. Update README and any remaining museum/count references.
7. Verify persistence, first-find behavior, silhouettes, grouped counts, and mobile digging-to-book flow.

## Relevant Files
- `js/data.js`: Site rosters, artifact metadata, `TOTAL_RELICS`, rank progression, and artifact lookup.
- `js/art.js`: Existing `PAINTERS`, `drawArtifact`, and `drawArtifactShadow`.
- `js/main.js`: Museum rendering, navigation, state collection lookup, totals, digging selection, and save persistence.
- `index.html`: Museum markup and navigation structure.
- `styles.css`: Museum and fixed mobile layout styles.
- `README.md`: Game documentation and feature counts.

## Important Context
- Changes remain uncommitted.
- `SITES[].artifacts` now contains 6 IDs per site.
- Existing collection entries contain `artifactId`, `condition`, `value`, and `buyer`.
- `window.__DUNE` exposes `state`, `showScreen`, `startDig`, `startClean`, `beginDig`, `sellRelic`, `save`, `digScene`, and `cleanScene`.
- `artifactImage(id, size)` and `drawArtifact(ctx, artifact.art, ...)` are the existing artwork paths.
- The museum count still needs to be reconciled from 12 to 24.

## Objective
- Complete and polish the mobile-first archaeological adventure with a functional collection book that clearly tracks all 24 relics.

## Requirements
- Add the collection book beside the Field tab’s recovered information, with a direct open button.
- Show exact black-outlined/black-silhouette artwork for undiscovered relics.
- Show discovered relics in normal procedural artwork.
- Allow the book to open reliably from Field and Museum.
- Preserve 24 total relics, unique discovery counts, duplicate-find behavior, and no-scrolling gameplay.

## Decisions
- Six relics per existing site; `TOTAL_RELICS = 24`.
- Each `SITES[].artifacts` roster remains the source of truth.
- Discovery derives from unique `state.collection[].artifactId` entries.
- The collection book should be accessible from Field and Museum.
- Discovered cards can open artifact detail modals.

- Expanded site rosters to 24 relic IDs and added collection metadata.

- Bound the Field and Museum book open/close controls.
- Added `/ 24` to Recovered and Museum totals.
- Fixed collection counts, duplicate-find handling, and JavaScript syntax checks.
- Identified that the current undiscovered CSS shape is only a generic black shape, not the artifact-specific silhouette.
- Changes remain uncommitted.

### Active
- Move the collection overlay outside Museum-only markup so it opens consistently across Field and Museum.
- Replace generic undiscovered card shapes with artifact-specific procedural black silhouettes.
- Verify the book opens from both entry points and updates after discoveries.

### Blocked
- (none)

1. Move `#collectionBook` to app-level markup instead of nesting it inside `#screen-museum`.
2. Generate each undiscovered silhouette with `drawArtifact` or an equivalent artifact-specific black mask.
3. Remove the broken generic `artifactSilhouette()` implementation or replace it with a working renderer.
4. Confirm discovered cards remain normal and undiscovered cards remain completely black.
5. Recheck 24 roster IDs, `artifactFor()` resolution, open/close behavior, mobile layout, and README/count references.

- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/README.md`: Project documentation and relic totals.

## Objective
- Complete and polish the mobile-first archaeological adventure, especially a collection book that clearly tracks all 24 unique relics.

## Requirements
- Preserve touch-first gameplay, fixed/no-scrolling layout, progression, economy, saves, and procedural artwork.
- Collection book must be accessible from Field and Museum.
- Undiscovered relic cards must show an exact artifact-specific black silhouette.
- Discovered relic cards must use normal procedural artwork and can open detail modals.
- Preserve 24 relics, unique discovery counts, duplicate-find behavior, first-dinar guarantee, and save key `dune_and_dust_save_v3`.

## Decisions
- Six relics per site; `TOTAL_RELICS = 24`.
- `SITES[].artifacts` remains the roster source of truth.
- Unique count derives from unique `state.collection[].artifactId`.
- Museum entry totals use collection-entry count; Field and collection-book totals use unique discovered IDs.
- Starting coins remain 620.
- Collection overlay should live at app level rather than inside Museum markup.

## Work State
### Completed
- Expanded rosters to 24 relic IDs and added collection metadata.
- Updated total references and collection counts to 24.
- Added Field and Museum collection-book entry buttons.
- Moved `#collectionBook` outside Museum markup to app-level markup.
- Replaced the generic CSS silhouette markup with procedural artifact silhouettes.
- Added `artifactSilhouette()` using `drawArtifact()` and a black composite mask.
- Rendered discovered cards with normal procedural images and undiscovered cards with silhouettes.
- Preserved found-card detail modal behavior.
- Verified JavaScript syntax with `node --check` for `main.js`, `data.js`, and `art.js`.
- Verified `git diff --check`.
- Changes remain uncommitted.

### Active
- Visually verify that all missing cards show exact silhouette shapes and that found cards switch to normal artwork.
- Verify opening and closing works from both Field and Museum.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run the app and verify both collection-book entry points open reliably.
2. Discover multiple items and confirm unique, duplicate, and per-site counts update correctly.
3. Recheck all 24 IDs and `artifactFor()` resolution.
4. Recheck mobile layout and ensure the collection overlay remains fixed with no gameplay scrolling regression.
5. Recheck README/count references and confirm no remaining 12-relic or generic-silhouette implementations.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/main.js`: Collection renderer, silhouettes, discovery counts, and book handlers.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/data.js`: 24-relic rosters and collection metadata.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/art.js`: Procedural `drawArtifact` painters.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: App-level collection overlay and Field/Museum entry markup.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css`: Overlay, card, and artifact-silhouette layout.

## Important Context
- `drawArtifact()` is the source for exact artifact-specific silhouettes.
- Discovered cards remain normal-color and can open accession records.
- Undiscovered cards must remain completely black and should not expose names or normal artwork.
- The collection count in `renderHome()` uses a `Set` of unique artifact IDs.
- Save key remains `dune_and_dust_save_v3`; starting coins remain 620.

## Objective
- Complete the mobile-first archaeological adventure’s 24-relic collection book.
- Fix the Field menu collection-book button, which the user reports still does nothing when pressed.

## Requirements
- Collection book must open from both Field and Museum.
- Undiscovered cards show exact artifact-specific black silhouettes; discovered cards show normal art and open detail records.
- Preserve touch-first gameplay, fixed layout, progression, economy, saves, and procedural artwork.
- Preserve 24 relics, unique discovery counts, duplicate-find behavior, first-dinar guarantee, save key `dune_and_dust_save_v3`, and 620 starting coins.

## Decisions
- Six relics per site; `TOTAL_RELICS = 24`; `SITES[].artifacts` is the roster source of truth.
- Unique counts derive from unique `state.collection[].artifactId`; Museum entry totals count collection entries.
- Collection overlay belongs at app level.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added 24 relic rosters, collection metadata, Field and Museum book buttons, and app-level collection overlay.
- Added procedural artifact silhouettes and found-card detail modals.
- Previous pass reported JavaScript syntax checks and `git diff --check` passed.
- Started a local server with `python3 -m http.server 4173`; no browser interaction test was completed.
- Changes remain uncommitted.

### Active
- Diagnose and fix the Field collection-book button’s reported no-op; listener exists, but live activation and overlay visibility have not been verified.

### Blocked
- Browser automation packages (`playwright`, `puppeteer`, `@playwright/test`, `playwright-core`) were not found in the attempted Node module resolution checks; live browser testing remains pending.

## Next Move
1. Reproduce the Field button failure in a browser and inspect console/runtime errors and hit testing.
2. Confirm click activation, `#collectionBook.hidden` changing, and overlay visibility; check Museum entry and close behavior too.
3. Fix the root cause, then rerun syntax checks and `git diff --check`.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: Field/Museum collection buttons and app-level overlay markup.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/main.js`: `renderCollectionBook()`, `artifactSilhouette()`, button event wiring in `bind()`, and `boot()`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css`: Field button and collection overlay layout/hit-target styling.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/data.js`: 24-relic rosters and `TOTAL_RELICS`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/art.js`: procedural artifact painters used for card artwork and silhouettes.

## Important Context
- Relevant symbols: `#openFieldCollectionBook`, `#openCollectionBook`, `#collectionBook`, `openCollectionBook`.
- `bind()` registers click listeners for both book-entry buttons; opening renders the book and sets `#collectionBook.hidden = false`.
- The Field button is in `index.html` inside `.home-lower`; its click listener appears in `js/main.js` around lines 996–1006. No root cause has been established yet.

## Objective
- Complete the mobile-first archaeological adventure’s collection-book behavior and enhance artifact presentation and private-sale flow.

## Requirements
- Collection book must open from both Field and Museum.
- Undiscovered cards show exact artifact-specific black silhouettes; discovered cards show normal art and open detail records.
- Preserve touch-first gameplay, fixed layout, progression, economy, saves, and procedural artwork.

- When selling to a private collector, send the artifact to an auction:
  - Show the artifact on a podium.
  - Show people gathered around it.
  - Bidders raise signs.
  - Track and display the bid amount.
- Artifact dirt appearance must remain consistent across discovery, digging, and cleaning:
  - It must look as dirty when excavated as it does at the start of cleaning.
  - It must not become more dirty, or suddenly become dirt-covered, after beginning cleaning.

- Six relics per site; `TOTAL_RELICS = 24`; `SITES[].artifacts` remains the roster source of truth.
